subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Give and take

options.text: A competition where the outcome is difficult to judge or predict
It seems likely, reasonable, or typical

solution:
The correct answer is "**Compromise, cooperation between people.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The idiom "give and take" refers to a situation where both parties involved are willing to compromise and cooperate with each other.**
 
• ऐसी स्थिति जहां शामिल दोनों पक्ष एक-दूसरे के साथ समझौता करने और सहयोग करने को तैयार हों।
 
 
• Example: There has to be a tremendous amount of give and take in negotiations.
 
 
 
• It implies a mutual exchange of concessions or benefits.
 
• The phrase is often used in the context of negotiations or relationships.
 
• Grammatically, "give and take" is a noun phrase, and it can be used as a standalone idiom or as part of a sentence.
 
• Thus, it is clear that the option 2 explains the given idiom correctly.

Hence,** the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Compromise" means an agreement that is reached when each person gets part, but not all, of what he/she wanted. (समझौता)
 
• "Cooperation" means an act or instance of working or acting together for a common purpose or benefit. (सहयोग)
